subject: AcreetionOS Update — July 25, 2026
body:
The AcreetionOS continuous integration pipeline has just been refined with the implementation of per-pipeline staging directories and relative symlinks for the latest.iso, significantly improving the efficiency and reliability of our ISO build process. This milestone is a result of the community's relentless efforts to streamline and stabilize our workflow, ensuring that users receive the most up-to-date and stable versions of AcreetionOS, which can be explored in more detail on our website at https://acreetionos.org/.

Development
The recent updates to our CI pipeline have been instrumental in reducing publish races between concurrent builds, and we're excited to see the positive impact this will have on our overall development process. Our team is committed to continuously refining and improving our infrastructure, and we're always looking for ways to enhance the user experience. For more information on our development process and how to get involved, please visit our documentation page at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html.

Community
The AcreetionOS community has been actively discussing the latest Emacs 31.1 release and its potential applications within our ecosystem. We're also keeping a close eye on the latest security updates and stable kernel sets, ensuring that our users have access to the latest and most secure software. To stay up-to-date with the latest news and discussions, please visit our wiki page at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html or check out our flash page at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html for the latest updates. 

Tip of the day
For users looking to stay current with the latest developments, we recommend checking out our changelog page at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html, which provides a detailed record of all updates and changes to the AcreetionOS system. By staying informed and engaged, users can take full advantage of the many benefits that AcreetionOS has to offer.
